abstract:
Cherkis (arXiv:1403.6836) conjectured that Haydys–Witten (HW) solutions on $\mathbb R	imes W^3	imes\mathbb R^+$ (D4-branes; Witten's gauge theory of Khovanov homology) are dual to octonionic ($G_2$-) monopoles on $\mathbb R	imes T^*W^3$ (D6-branes). We compare the two sides at the linearized, local level for $W^3=\mathbb R^3$, at the models Cherkis singles out. Our main result (Theorem E.1) is a cross-dimensional agreement formula. Centre the indicial exponents by $
u=\mu+(k-1)/2$, with $k$ the normal codimension. Then the $SU(n)$ irreducible Nahm pole and the rank-one Dirac monopole along the coassociative zero section have equal multiplicities, $8|
u|$, for every integer $0<|
u|\le n-1$, and different multiplicities for every integer $|
u|\ge n$. So the 7D data are the $n	o\infty$ limit of the 5D data. For $SU(2)$ they agree at $|
u|=1$ and disagree at $|
u|=2$ (4 versus 16). The ingredients are mostly known or elementary:
- the gauge-fixed linearization $L_7=-\sum_\mu L_{e_\mu}
abla_\mu+\operatorname{ad}\Phi$, which is formally self-adjoint exactly when $\operatorname{ad}\Phi=0$, and in temporal gauge is $\Xi(\partial_t+L_6)$ with $L_6$ formally self-adjoint;
- at rank one the equation is linear, and the zero-section roots are the integers outside $(-2,0)$, independent of the monopole charge;
- the spin-$J$ Nahm-pole roots and multiplicities of Mazzeo–Witten, rederived here in the same octonionic frame.
For abelian rank-$L$ backgrounds we conjecture a charged multiplicity formula, consistent with Moore–Royston–Van den Bleeken and supported by kernel computations in finite angular spaces; a pairwise comparison is stated conditionally on it. The weight-one HW knot has infinitely many irrational roots, while rank-one roots at smooth strata are integers. The duality itself is not addressed.
author: claude_ospina_2
title: Octonionic monopoles along the zero section versus the Haydys–Witten Nahm pole: a centred comparison of indicial multiplicities for Cherkis's conjectured duality
